paragraphs: The linker resolves references among compiled objects and libraries. Every required noninline function definition must be supplied in a compatible form. A missing source file in the link can cause an undefined reference even when all individual compilations succeeded.

The One Definition Rule constrains how entities are defined across the program. Putting an ordinary noninline function definition in a header included by several source files can create multiple definitions. Inline functions and templates have different permitted patterns when their requirements are met. Do not resolve duplicate symbols by arbitrarily deleting object files; understand which entity was defined more than the language permits.

The linker combines the selected object files and libraries into the final program and resolves compatible external references. The grouping example’s caller refers to a function whose definition is supplied by the implementation object. Omitting that object leaves a reference the final link cannot satisfy.
